primary_sources.title: Little q-Legendre polynomials and irrationality of certain Lambert series
primary_sources.author: Walter Van Assche
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Introduction, Lemma 1: if integral forms b_n x-a_n are nonzero and tend to zero, then x is irrational. Sections 2-3 construct little-q-Legendre Pade approximants, integerize them, and compare denominator growth with remainder decay.
primary_sources.supports: The precise classical qualitative consumer and its placement inside the closest little-q-Legendre Lambert-series method.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The local two-selector determinant inequality, the four tail-start cost table, or the 3/2 rational-base programme.

primary_sources.title: q-Apery Irrationality Proofs by q-WZ Pairs
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Sections 1.3-1.6 define the q-WZ mollifier, summed numerator/denominator sequences, and scalar recurrence; Section 1.7 proves integerization and compares the denominator-height estimate with the approximation error before Theorem 1.
primary_sources.supports: The source q-Apery architecture from which the local selector rows and height/decay question arise.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Generic unimodular recombination of two selector rows, the determinant-forced coefficient-height bound, or a rational-base 3/2 theorem.

primary_sources.title: A refinement of Nesterenko's linear independence criterion with applications to zeta values
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Introduction, Theorem A, states Nesterenko's coefficient-growth versus small-linear-form criterion; Theorem 1 and Corollaries 1-2 incorporate common divisors of coefficients, explicitly motivated by hypergeometric and q-analog constructions.
primary_sources.supports: The conventional modern framework for balancing coefficient height, linear-form decay, and arithmetic content.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The elementary local constant 2, the two-selector finite data, or the conclusion that this particular recombination route fails.

mechanism_comparison.classical_core: At a rational target a nonzero integral linear form has a denominator-sized gap, so a nonzero sequence tending to zero proves irrationality. Quantitative criteria balance coefficient growth, arithmetic content, and decay.
mechanism_comparison.local_generalization: Two simultaneous forms carry an exterior determinant. A unimodular change of basis preserves that determinant, so simultaneous smallness imposes an explicit coefficient-height cost.
mechanism_comparison.source_specific_delta: The exact finite chain first shows modular selectors outside both algebraic nullspaces, then shows their normalized real remainders exceed one at starts 1 through 4, and finally repairs starts 0 through 3 by putting the real coordinate into the lattice objective. The determinant receipt shows that at start 3 at least 1874 of the observed 2261 coefficient bits are structurally forced.
mechanism_comparison.logical_boundary: Continued fractions can find finite small combinations, but an all-start theorem making both integral forms tend to zero would itself be an irrationality proof. It cannot be treated as a generic auxiliary lemma independent of the endpoint.
